title: Question 3.1b: Understanding Method Chaining
instruction: This code uses a pattern called "method chaining" where multiple methods are called on the same object in sequence.
reveal: This is called method chaining. Each method (like `.setInputCol()` and `.setOutputCol()`) returns the same object, so you can call another method on the result. This is equivalent to writing: `Tokenizer tokenizer = new Tokenizer(); tokenizer.setInputCol("text"); tokenizer.setOutputCol("words");` but more compact. This pattern is common in Java libraries that build configuration objects.
